speaker: character
text: We'd love to fund your club for a whole year: books, snacks, everything. We'd just turn it into a coding club for kids, with our logo on it. Can you give me a yes by tomorrow?

speaker: candidate
text: Yes, we'll take it! Send the contract.

speaker: character
text: Honestly, nobody funds reading clubs anymore. Coding is what parents want. Why hold on to the old idea?

speaker: candidate
text: Honestly, whatever gets funded is fine. Money is money.

speaker: character
text: Look, I have two other clubs that would say yes in a second. I need your answer today.

speaker: candidate
text: Okay, okay, yes, don't go to anyone else. We'll do whatever you want.

speaker: character
text: So what could work for you? I still need something to show my boss.

speaker: candidate
text: Let's just become the coding club and drop reading.

speaker: character
text: And your volunteers, will they go along with this? Who decides on your side?

speaker: candidate
text: I'll tell the volunteers about the money but not the logo part.

speaker: character
text: Okay, a smaller deal could work. But I need it in writing. What goes in it?

speaker: candidate
text: Just tell me where to sign. I don't need to read it.

speaker: character
text: I heard two parents complained that the club is becoming an advert for us. My boss is nervous. What are you going to do?

speaker: candidate
text: It's our club, not theirs. They'll get over it.
